desc.about: {{BRAND_NAME}} is a student project from Brandenburg. Why the app exists and what you may do with it.

areas.title: Timetable
areas.text: Week A and B, double periods, single periods or your own times. {{BRAND_NAME}} shows the current and next lesson with the room.

areas.title: Grades
areas.text: Points from 0 to 15 or grades from 1 to 6, depending on your year. {{BRAND_NAME}} works out each subject's average, exams count a third.

areas.title: Homework and tests
areas.text: Homework, tests and exams with a countdown. Tasks get a due date and one of three priorities.

areas.title: IServ
areas.text: Sign in once with your IServ account. {{BRAND_NAME}} then fetches your assignments and the substitution plan on its own, and on the computer your IServ mail too. On Android, events come in as well, and new messages show up as notifications.

areas.title: Transit
areas.text: Connections with live delays and platforms. The way to school and back home is one tap away.

areas.title: Calendar
areas.text: Your own events and the school holidays and public holidays of all 16 German states, without typing them in. On Android, events from IServ come in too.

areas.title: Luna
areas.text: Luna is the assistant in {{BRAND_NAME}}. Ask her what is on tomorrow, tell her „Maths p. 38 for Monday“ and she adds the homework. Before an exam she builds you a study plan.

macos: On first launch macOS blocks the app because it isn't signed by Apple. Go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click “Open Anyway”.
steps.macos_terminal: Or paste this into Terminal, the script installs the app into /Applications:
windows: If your browser warns that the file is rarely downloaded, choose “Keep”.
If Windows SmartScreen warns you, click “More info” and “Run anyway”.
{{BRAND_NAME}} installs without admin rights and opens by itself.
linux: Double-click the .deb file to install {{BRAND_NAME}} through your software center, or run this in your Downloads folder: sudo apt install ./{{BRAND_NAME}}-*.deb
Then open {{BRAND_NAME}} from your app menu.
android: Open the APK and allow installs from this source.
{{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when an update is ready.
ios: Open the web app in Safari.
There, tap Share {share}, then “Add to Home Screen”.
From now on, start {{BRAND_NAME}} from the new icon and set it up there. What you enter in the Safari tab doesn't carry over.
web: Open the link and {{BRAND_NAME}} runs right in your browser.
Your data lives in this browser's storage.

privacy_page.title: What {{BRAND_NAME}} does with your data

privacy_page.lock_text: {{BRAND_NAME}} stores your IServ and mail login details encrypted, on the computer with Fernet and a key from 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds, on Android in the system's encrypted storage. On the computer, {{BRAND_NAME}} encrypts grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, events, notes, mail drafts, saved places and your history with Luna the same way. Not encrypted there are the timetable with subjects, teachers, rooms and times, the task list, training, Pomodoro statistics, reviews, bookmarks, tickets, the cached substitution plan and the settings with your birthday and weather location, and on Android and in the web app everything except the login details. All of it stays on your device.
privacy_page.lock_number_label: PBKDF2 rounds for your login details on the computer
no: Tracking, usage analytics or crash reports
privacy_page.open_title: You don't have to take my word for it
privacy_page.open_text: Anyone can read the source code of {{BRAND_NAME}}. Every line that touches your data is public on GitHub.

download_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} stays free, even once the beta is over. You don't need an account; you can start right after the download.

faq.a: No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is free for you, and its source code is public on GitHub. There are no paid features or subscriptions.

faq.q: Do I have to type in my timetable?
faq.a: Yes, once. {{BRAND_NAME}} can't fetch it from IServ or WebUntis. The setup in the app walks you through it in a few minutes.

faq.q: I already have IServ and WebUntis. What does {{BRAND_NAME}} add?
faq.a: IServ and WebUntis each know only their own part. {{BRAND_NAME}} shows you on one screen which lesson is next and in which room, and what's left to do before your next test. {{BRAND_NAME}} doesn't know about cancellations in WebUntis, you still see those there.
On Android, the Mac, Windows and Linux, {{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when a new version is out. You download it here.

faq.q: Why isn't {{BRAND_NAME}} in the App Store or on Google Play?
faq.a: I distribute {{BRAND_NAME}} directly, without store fees and with faster updates. That's why the iPhone gets the web app.

faq.q: Can I move my data to a new device?
faq.a: Yes, with a backup. In the settings under Daten (data), you save your timetable and subjects, grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, tasks, events, notes, places and settings to a file and read it in on the new device. You set up training, bookmarks and your IServ and mail logins there again. There is no cloud that keeps your devices in sync by itself.
No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is an independent student project. It only uses your IServ account to sign in on your behalf.
Not yet. The app itself is in German, it was built for German schools.

about_page.title: A student project from Brandenburg
about_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} is built by a student from Brandenburg, currently in the final years of school. The app started as a tool for their own school day and is now there for anyone looking for something similar.
story: For school, my calendar, the bus and my homework I had a separate app each. None of them knew about the others.
{{BRAND_NAME}} brings that together: the timetable knows which room is next, tests sit with a countdown among your deadlines, and the bus home is one tap away.
Everything runs on your device. I don't want to see your grades, and I can't.

privacy_policy.s1_p1: The data controller within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:
privacy_policy.s2_p1: {{BRAND_NAME}} was built on a "Local-First" principle. This means: All data you enter in the App is stored exclusively on your device and is not transmitted to servers of the Provider. Third-party services receive it only when you use a feature that needs them, such as transit or weather. The App also makes some requests by itself, for example to check for updates. Section 3 lists these services.
privacy_policy.s2_p2: We do not collect, store, or process any personal data through the App, unless you use features that require an internet connection (e.g., real-time public transit data) or the App makes one of the requests listed in Section 3 d) by itself.
privacy_policy.s3_sub1_p1: All data you enter (timetables, grades, tasks, training data, notes, etc.) is stored exclusively on your device. The App stores login details, for example for IServ and email, in encrypted form. In the apps for computers, this also applies to grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, events, notes, mail drafts, saved places and the assistant's history. Stored unencrypted in a local database there are the timetable with subjects, teachers, rooms and times, the task list, training data, Pomodoro statistics, reviews, bookmarks, tickets and the settings, which include your birthday and weather location. The cached substitution plan is also stored there unencrypted. On Android and in the web app, all data except the login details is stored unencrypted. The Provider has no access to this data at any time.
privacy_policy.s3_sub2_p1: When you use the transit feature, the App sends requests to Transitous (api.transitous.org) and, for ticket prices in Berlin and Brandenburg, to transport.rest (v6.vbb.transport.rest). These requests contain the stops, addresses and times of your search. If you have saved your home or your school as a place, connections from or to there also include its location, and “In der Nähe” (nearby) includes your current location if you allow it. In the older views of the computer app, requests also go to transport.rest and, for fares, to Deutsche Bahn. No device IDs are transmitted.
privacy_policy.s3_sub3_p1: {{BRAND_NAME}} contains no analytics, no tracking, no crash reporters, and no telemetry. No usage statistics are collected whatsoever.
privacy_policy.s3_sub4_p1: The App contacts the following services when you use the feature in question. It makes the requests marked “by itself” without any action on your part. As with any connection, the service sees your IP address.
privacy_policy.s3_list1: Your school's IServ: your username and password to sign in, then the requests for mail, substitution plan, assignments, events and messages (not in the web app)
privacy_policy.s3_list2: Your email provider: login details and mail, directly via IMAP and SMTP (apps for computers)
privacy_policy.s3_list3: Open-Meteo: the place you want the weather for, or the location of your home
